project.name: OpenRound grip-end sensor tag research packet

coordinate_system.origin: PCB reference origin or measured tag center of mass; freeze the choice before CAD release
coordinate_system.axes: right-handed; +Z follows the club shaft toward the clubhead, +X and +Y are fixed to the PCB reference; field orientation is not repeatable unless the grip interface indexes the tag

requirements.statement: The final tag shall target 9-10 g mass and shall not exceed 12 g.
The grip interface shall be sized from a caliper survey of every supported grip; the CAD 13.5 mm hole value is a placeholder and is not a release dimension.
Each passive club dock shall use a measured two-piece split collar around the upper grip with a keyed dovetail and captive spring tab; counterweighted grips are unsupported until separately measured.
requirements.source: mechanical/design.json#requirements (public design requirement; physical validation pending)

requirements.statement: The final body shall use a heat- and UV-suitable candidate material; ASA is the current candidate, while PETG is limited to room-temperature rig iterations.

The reusable puck shall preserve an event until the phone has durably stored and acknowledged it; event identity shall include puck identity, boot epoch, and monotonic sequence, with mount-session club assignment kept as separate provenance.
requirements.source: mechanical/design.json#requirements (public design requirement; physical validation pending)

requirements.statement: The Phase 1 rig shall rigidly couple the sensors to the club so that compliant mounting material does not filter the shock spectrum under study.
No fit, pull-out, shock, waterproof, power, radio, or field-accuracy claim shall be promoted to release status without attended physical evidence.
The sensor PCB shall be hard-located in a rigid carrier; TPU may be used only as a non-structural liner, bumper, or gasket and shall not be the sole sensor load path.
requirements.source: mechanical/design.json#requirements (public design requirement; physical validation pending)

requirements.statement: The active puck shall be reusable across supported club docks, and the first club-assignment workflow shall require explicit user confirmation when the mount session changes.
requirements.source: mechanical/design.json#requirements (public design requirement; physical validation pending)

interfaces.name: grip butt interface
interfaces.description: Upper-grip and butt-cap exterior for the two-piece passive dock; diameter, depth, ovality, cap OD, and obstructions vary across the bag.

interfaces.name: sensor platform
interfaces.description: Rigid PCB-to-body seat for the XIAO/high-g Phase 1 rig; no foam, rubber, or tape under the boards.

interfaces.name: battery door
interfaces.description: Replaceable CR2032 with lid preload and a candidate radial O-ring; exact gland and contact geometry remain to be tested.

interfaces.name: BLE and phone sync
interfaces.description: Connectable puck event log, GATT read/ack, mount-session provenance, phone breadcrumb, and raw capture export.

interfaces.name: reusable puck and passive dock
interfaces.description: Keyed dovetail and captive spring tab between one active puck carrier and each passive split collar; no electronics in the dock.

load_cases.name: swing and impact shock
load_cases.description: Grip-end acceleration and shock spectrum during real strikes, practice swings, fat/turf-brush swings, bag jostles, and drops.
load_cases.input: Unknown until the high-g reference channel is measured on the Phase 1 rig.

load_cases.name: dock retention and pull-out
load_cases.description: Attach/detach cycle and pull-out behavior of each supported passive dock size.
load_cases.target: The first fit coupon requires at least 20 attach/detach cycles; the production dock target is at least 100 cycles and a 50 N pull-out check. These are test targets, not demonstrated strength.

load_cases.name: battery contact interruption
load_cases.description: Coin-cell contact bounce during representative impact and shock.
load_cases.input: Waveform and contact geometry unknown until the battery-door prototype is instrumented.

tolerances.value: TBD from two-axis caliper survey and printed split-collar fit coupons
Must not exceed the smallest supported grip butt outside diameter; final numeric limit is measured per grip

hazards: Club-mounted mass can alter swing feel or detach during a swing.
Coin-cell contacts and prototype Li-Po wiring can fail under shock.
Printed material and cell temperature limits can be exceeded in a parked vehicle.
High-g shock and swinging clubs require an attended, controlled test area.
gates: Require attended approval before power, motion, fabrication, or physical testing.
Verify fit coupons on a non-critical club before full rig installation.
Keep the Li-Po prototype off the club when not actively supervised; do not leave it in a hot vehicle.
Do not swing a prototype until retention, mass, clearance, and battery retention are inspected.
Do not treat a geometry render, packet validation, or offline classifier result as proof of physical safety or accuracy.
Human owner must review field evidence before release or full-bag deployment.
